title: 2 festive traps that cost you in January #Debt
text:
In Wonga's survey, more than one in five people planned to use credit for the festive season. A store card or buy now, pay later feels free in December, but the first payment arrives in January on top of everything else. Before you swipe, ask: will I still be paying for this at Easter? And if you're short in January, a loan from an unregistered lender can cost far more than you think. The National Credit Regulator's advice: only borrow from registered credit providers, and check a lender on its website.

Full guide: "Festive Season on a Budget: How Not to Start January Broke (South Africa 2026)" on the Money From Zero channel.
